feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content reflects real scope across strategy, platforms, and operations. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong career progression at NACo and a well-aligned headline/profile.  
- Good credibility through specific platforms, tools, and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain relevance in digital strategy, governance, and advocacy communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: show results such as growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to tighten structure and improve scannability.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); keep punctuation style consistent in bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding your most recent strengths in digital transformation, governance, and mission-driven communications would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel strategy, and operational systems for complex organizations.
- Make the final sentence more specific by linking advocacy/policy messaging to audience clarity and stakeholder alignment.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Experienced in advocacy and policy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex technical issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “workflows and systems” overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro high-level and let skills sections carry the detail.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy, platforms, operations, analytics, advocacy, multimedia.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use either “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” consistently with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “workflows and systems,” “advocacy messaging”).
- Also duplicates Topline Skills and Soft Skills, especially analytics, stakeholder coordination, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Serve as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics processes to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add usage, launch count, or stakeholder reach if available.
- Tighten technical/AI bullets: “Delivered CMS/front-end enhancements for high-traffic public sites and led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite example already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct results.
- Governance/analytics language repeats the summary and NACo role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and operational scale.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes:
- “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”
- “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making.”
- “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either add stronger results or cut it.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; keep this version at the enterprise/leadership level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution leadership, channel ownership, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging ahead of promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Owned production and distribution of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across web, email and social.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership strengths rather than generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector stakeholder messaging  
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Change management for complex publishing organizations” if targeting enterprise digital leadership roles.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid broad terms like “leadership” and “planning” unless paired with a specific domain.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for experience bullets rather than this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat language already used in the header and core competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is also reinforced in multiple NACo roles and recent projects.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent web modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, and AI-enabled search; move older or less central platforms later or remove.
- Consider dropping one lower-signal platform here (for example SharePoint or Power Pages) unless it is important for target roles.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “API-driven platform integrations” instead of generic nouns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full platform list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; mention it once here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & dashboarding • KPI framework development • Executive reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership-level event delivery rather than generic task skills.

- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with broader event-delivery language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant, recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or drop it if space is tight.
- If formatting allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency.
- If you want more impact, align with recent work: **Drupal-focused enterprise web platforms, plus WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid listing the exact same platforms in both places without added context.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery”
- Consider adding brief qualifiers where true: “JavaScript (front-end enhancements), API integrations (CMS/workflow), GitHub Actions (deployment automation), Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting)”
- If space allows, replace older/generic terms with higher-value specifics tied to recent work, e.g. “structured search implementation” or “deployment automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GTM overlaps somewhat with analytics/infrastructure themes elsewhere, so keep it only if you’ve used it hands-on.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already named elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems/automation over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Consider adding light functional framing: **Automation & workflow design:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Drop weaker/older tools unless they are current differentiators; keeping 6–8 tools will feel sharper than a long list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Basecamp may feel dated and lower-priority versus more recent enterprise tools already shown.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership profile, but this line is too bare and doesn’t reflect level of use or business context. It would be stronger if framed around campaign/email operations rather than just listing vendor names.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these were hands-on systems used recently; otherwise order by recency/relevance.
- If space allows, add light context: **Email marketing, member engagement and newsletter operations: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in the NACo or consulting roles, place it first and consider dropping the least-used tool to keep the list credible and focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not already covered there.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t repeat analytics/automation concepts already covered in other Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, promotion, and any concrete outputs without repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit
- Lead with advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make contributions more concrete: specify the website refresh scope, cadence of weekly video updates, number/type of livestreams, or audience/reach if known.
- Use sharper action verbs and trim filler: replace “supporting the creation of” / “strengthening workflows” with “helped launch” / “standardized.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized workflows across web, email, social and multimedia, produced recurring weekly video updates and livestreamed key events, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on launching/establishing the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; frame this as early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch and scope, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business support language: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and program content development.”
- Tighten multimedia wording: “Produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications” instead of “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences served, programs supported, or types of deliverables produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later NACo roles already show stronger video/digital leadership.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is broad and may repeat later advocacy/editorial coordination language.
